title: Structural Micro-Pattern Color of Picea pungens Epicuticular Wax
content: The properties of plant epicuticular waxes which are multifunctional materials governed by their chemical composition and structural organization. The latter is particularly important for the optical response of wax coatings. Here, the optical and structural properties of crystalline epicuticular wax from Picea pungens needles were investigated using optical and scanning electron microscopy. Under reflected-light scheme, we observe brightly colored microdomains ranging from red to blue, with their apparent color varying depending on the illumination and observation geometry. The wax crystallites are nanotubes that form clusters characterized by preferential nanotube alignment. A comparative analysis of optical and scanning electron microscopy of the same wax fragments revealed a relationship between microdomains coloration and the spatial organization of nanotube clusters, including their packing density and preferential orientation. Modifications to cluster morphology are accompanied by changes in the observed microdomain colors. At the macroscopic scale, the transmission and small-angle scattering spectra have neither maxima nor minima across the visible spectral range, whereas the intensity of small-angle scattered light increases towards shorter wavelengths. The results obtained may be promising for the development of natural or bio-inspired materials whose optical and spectral properties are determined by the packing density and spatial orientation of nanocrystals.
